references.text: Contains the detailed laws about clean and unclean animals that define what is 'abominable' to eat, as summarized in Deuteronomy 14:3
Distinguishes between clean and unclean animals and links this to holiness, using similar terminology about separating the clean from the unclean
Ezekiel declares that he has never eaten anything abominable, using the same Hebrew word 'toevah' (abominable)
The priests shall not eat anything that dies of itself or is torn by beasts, which expands on the principle of avoiding abominable food
The immediate context specifying which animals are permitted and forbidden to eat, and elaborating what 'abominable' entails
Peter refuses to eat unclean animals but is told that God has cleansed them, illustrating the New Testament interpretation of these dietary laws
